writeup: TIC 229401461 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 79.01 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.04%, with a detection significance of 58.0 in the BLS periodogram. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms the signal at a peak signal-to-noise of 100.8, though the centroid offset of 18.8 arcseconds from the target warrants attention. The secondary eclipse was not detected. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and the pipeline's machine-learning model assigns it a high probability score of 0.98. However, the eclipses show significantly alternating depths, suggesting the true period may be twice the initially measured value; the corrected period of 79.01 days is reported here. No secondary eclipse detection and the centroid offset remain open questions about this candidate system.
